title: Rewrite n sin theta = (n-1) cos theta as tan theta = k and give n k
stem: Express \({n|int}\sin\theta={m|int}\cos\theta\) in the form \(\tan\theta=k\). Give the value of \({n|int}k\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: Divide both sides by n cos theta, provided cos theta is not zero.

title: Number of solutions of tan n x = 1 in 0 to 180 degrees
source: Theory P1-5.8 Quick check 2; n solutions of tan n x = 1 for 0 < x < 180
stem: How many solutions of \(\tan({n|int}x)=1\) are there for \(0^\circ<x<180^\circ\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: \({n|int}x\) runs through an open interval of length \({n|int}\times 180^\circ\), and \(\tan\phi=1\) has one solution in each interval of \(180^\circ\), so there are \({A|int}\) solutions.
steps.note: One solution of tan phi = 1 in each 180 degrees.

contexts.note: Includes the original tan 3x = 1, three solutions

title: Number of solutions of tan n x = sqrt 3 in 0 to 180 degrees
source: Theory P1-5.8 Quick check 3; n solutions of tan n x = sqrt 3 for 0 < x < 180
stem: How many solutions of \(\tan({n|int}x)=\sqrt{{3}}\) are there for \(0^\circ<x<180^\circ\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: \({n|int}x\) runs through an open interval of length \({n|int}\times 180^\circ\), and \(\tan\phi=\sqrt{{3}}\) has one solution in each interval of \(180^\circ\), so there are \({A|int}\) solutions.
steps.note: One solution of tan phi = sqrt 3 in each 180 degrees.

contexts.note: Includes the original tan 2x = sqrt 3, two solutions

title: A tangent equation and a further equation in 2x

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
(i) Express the equation \(3\sin\theta=\cos\theta\) in the form \(\tan\theta=k\) and solve the equation for \(0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ\). [2]

(ii) Solve the equation \(3\sin^2 2x=\cos^2 2x\) for \(0^\circ<x<180^\circ\). [4]

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: A1, ignore solutions outside the range 0 → 180.

steps.name: s3
steps.text_tex: (ii) \(\tan 2x=\pm\dfrac{{1}}{{\sqrt{{3}}}}\), or an equivalent statement that a square root is needed.
steps.note: Official MS: Must be sq. root soi; sin 2x = (+/-)1/2 or cos 2x = (+/-)sqrt(3)/2 using c^2+s^2=1; Not tan x = (+/-)1/sqrt(3).

steps.name: s5
steps.note: Official MS: A1, any correct second value (75, 105, 165).

steps.name: s6
steps.note: Official MS: A1, cao. All four correct. Extra solns in range -1.

title: An equation involving sine and tangent

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: M1, for use of tan theta = sin theta / cos theta. BOD if theta missing.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: M1 WWW. Factorise, not divide by sin theta or tan theta. May see tan theta (4 cos theta + 1) or sin theta (4 + sec theta).

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: A1, AWRT 104.5 degrees (1.82 rads A0). Ignore answers outside (0, 180). If M1 M0, SC B1 for 104.5, max 2/3.
